Type normally in the Magic Box to find local files, search the web, or hand the query to an AI app you choose.
Type a web address to open it directly; other plain text remains a web or AI query.
Your last five successful searches and ? app launches stay on this device. Reuse one, delete one, or clear them all from the empty Magic Box.

This replaces Gemini, Bixby, or your current default assistant until you change it back in Android settings.
Mink Assistant ignores assist context and does not request microphone, call-log, screen-reading, or screen-context access.

Mink walks, moves steadily, gets distracted, checks a phone, rests, or goes to sleep based on today’s local activity and the time of day.

Other apps are excluded from the trail. %1$s never sends tracked activity, app choices, or insights to Katoa Apps.

Tap the chat icon beside Settings to read active message and email threads. Inline reply appears only when the originating app supplies Android’s reply action.

Swipe right from Home for local daily insights. Swipe left or use Back to return Home.
Each configurable slot keeps its built-in default until you assign an app. Its app icon then takes over on Home.
Long-press any Home shortcut to enter edit mode, then drag shortcuts into your preferred order.
%1$s does not keep conversation history. Message text and replies remain in memory and are never sent to Katoa Apps.

Only read when you search for a person.

Android will show Contacts and Call prompts next. If Mink Assistant is active and your messaging choice includes direct SMS, Android may grant or request Send SMS access before the optional Conversations and Mink’s Day explanations. Media access appears only when you enable file search.
Call access is used only when you choose Call now. Choose calling app hands the number to an Android-compatible dialer instead.
Send SMS access is used only after you choose a contact, write a message, and press the @ action. Always ask adds a separate confirmation; Always send treats that action as approval.
Optional accessibility access performs only Android’s Lock screen action after your double-tap. It cannot read screen content or observe what you do.
Optional access searches photo, video, and audio filenames locally.
Optional notification access powers message and email conversations. Other notification types are ignored, and you can revoke access whenever you want.
Optional Usage Access measures foreground time and opens for your tracked social apps only, entirely on this device.
Samsung Weather missing? Turn on Settings > Apps > Samsung app settings > Weather settings > Show Weather on Apps screen, then return here.
Choose a document folder to search. You can add or remove folders later in Settings.
%1$s searches only folders you approve through Android.
Search queries and filenames stay on your device and are never sent to us.
Android’s Usage Access lets %1$s measure when your tracked social apps are in the foreground and for how long.
%1$s uses this only to calculate today’s Mink state and insights on your device. It does not upload your activity, sell it, or keep a separate usage-history database.
This is optional. Mink’s page still works as a time-of-day companion if you skip it, and you can revoke access whenever you want.

To make double-tap behave like the power button, %1$s uses Android’s accessibility Lock screen action.
The service runs only when you double-tap empty Home space. It does not observe accessibility events, read screen content, perform gestures, or collect data.
Android will ask you to enable Double-tap screen lock. You can disable it at any time in Accessibility settings.
Your phone’s assistant gesture will open the keyboard-first Magic Box over your current app.
Choosing %1$s replaces your current default digital assistant. You can switch back at any time in system settings.

Mink Assistant does not request microphone, call-log, screen-reading, or screen-context access. Android may grant Send SMS as part of the assistant role; %1$s uses it only after you choose a recipient, write the message, and press the @ action.
Android notification access lets %1$s read active message and email notifications, group them into conversations, and offer inline reply when the originating app provides a reply action.
Notifications outside messages and email are ignored. Conversation contents and replies are kept in memory only. They are not stored by %1$s, uploaded, or sent to Katoa Apps.
Replies are handed directly to the app that created the notification. You can revoke access at any time in Android settings.
